questions.text: Which of Garvin's 8 dimensions asks 'does the product meet its written specification?'
questions.explanation: Conformance measures whether a product or service matches its defined specification — for example, whether a data record contains all required fields in the correct format.

questions.text: Quality Control (QC) differs from Quality Assurance (QA) in that QC:
options: Detects defects after they occur by inspecting output
Prevents defects by redesigning the process
Is only applied to manufacturing, not software
questions.explanation: QC is reactive — it inspects output to find defects that have already been produced. QA is proactive — it improves the process to stop defects from occurring.

questions.text: An ETL pipeline produces records that pass all schema validation checks but compute incorrect benefit amounts because the transformation formula is wrong. Which best describes this situation?
options: High conformance quality, low performance quality
Low conformance quality, high performance quality
Both high — schema validation guarantees correctness
Both low — any error means all dimensions are poor
questions.explanation: The pipeline conforms to its schema specification (conformance quality is high) but fails at its primary job of computing correct values (performance quality is low). These two dimensions are independent.

questions.text: A health insurer scores high on 'Perceived Quality' but low on 'Conformance'. Which best explains how this is possible?
options: Customers trust the brand based on past reputation, even though current processes fail specifications
Perceived quality is always equal to conformance quality
High marketing spend always raises conformance
ISO 9001 certification guarantees high perceived quality
questions.explanation: Perceived quality is driven by reputation, brand image, and historical trust — it can lag behind actual current performance. A well-regarded insurer may have declining conformance while retaining high perceived quality temporarily.

questions.text: ISO 9001 is a quality management standard that prescribes specific statistical tools every organisation must use.
questions.explanation: ISO 9001 specifies requirements for a quality management system (customer focus, documentation, management review, continual improvement) but does NOT prescribe which specific tools to use. Organisations choose appropriate methods for their context.
